Descent line (Sawtooth Pass vs reversing the ascent)

before.descent_text: Most parties reverse the ascent line rather than descending a different route. Downclimb off the summit block through the gully system back to the base of Mount Lincoln, regain the Sawtooth Ridge crest, and follow it southwest back to Sawtooth Pass, then downclimb/glissade (early season) the open snow-and-rock slope back to the Gladys Divide trail near the small tarn at ~4,400 ft. From there it's a long but straightforward hike back through Flapjack Lakes and down the Flapjack Lakes Trail / North Fork Skokomish River Trail to Staircase. This is a walk-off/downclimb — no fixed rappel stations, bolted anchors, or documented rope-descent points were found for the standard scramble route, so rappels = 0. The crux is reversing the airy class 3+ (occasional class-4-feeling move) terrain right off the summit block and negotiating chockstones/ledges partway down the gully; a short handline for less-experienced party members on this section is a reasonable precaution some parties use, but it is not a technical anchor-and-rope rappel. Primary descent hazards: route-finding (several similar-looking gully systems seam the south face — parties have reported descending the wrong chute/chockstone gully and encountering sketchy downclimbing before regaining the correct line or Madeline Creek drainage), loose rock/choss on the ridge and gully walls, and lingering snow on the Sawtooth Pass slope into midsummer (ice axe useful into July). Plan for a long day — trip reports commonly cite 11–14+ hours car-to-car — and carry a headlamp and extra water for the trail miles back to Staircase.
